builder_plan.scenario: Your self-hosted model spends too long generating answers token by token.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a compatible draft model and serving integration exist before renting compute.
builder_plan.baseline: The same target with speculation off, then your existing drafter if you have one.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted draft length, tokens per second, tail latency, output quality, and total GPU cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: TraceSpec: Understanding and Improving Speculative Decoding for LLM Agents
summary: Replaces aggregate speculative-decoding metrics and fixed full-turn draft supervision with trajectory-conditioned training that allocates prediction budget based on prefix-aware acceptance gaps. Costs include training on intermediate assistant turns, maintaining state-conditioned estimators, and instrumenting fixed-prefix replay evaluation. Can fail if workload phases or trajectory conditions differ from the browsing and software-engineering traces used for validation, making the adaptive allocation miscalibrated.
rationale: The method targets draft-model supervision rather than requiring new infrastructure, but its gains depend on matching the reader's specific agent workload phases and require validation on their own trajectories before production adoption.
technique: State-conditioned adaptive draft allocation for speculative decoding

claims.statement: Replaces aggregate speculative-decoding metrics and fixed full-turn draft supervision with trajectory-conditioned training that allocates prediction budget based on prefix-aware acceptance gaps. Costs include training on intermediate assistant turns, maintaining state-conditioned estimators, and instrumenting fixed-prefix replay evaluation. Can fail if workload phases or trajectory conditions differ from the browsing and software-engineering traces used for validation, making the adaptive allocation miscalibrated.
Improves replay throughput by 12.5% to 22.6% over DSpark base; ablations show 3.3% to 10.0% accepted-length increase over fixed full-turn supervision.
